summary: Post-Monday fix round: tip pools + tax invoices per company, kitchen/admin consistency, books guards + catch-up, bookings/SMTP/fiscal screens, cancelled-ticket card refunds — build, adversarial review, fix

built.summary:
All three items are fixed. The new tests (22) pass, and so do 14 existing suites that touch these files (186 passed, 4 skipped). Typechecks are clean for backend and frontend/admin. The tablet has no node_modules, so I typechecked tablet/app/(staff)/reservations.tsx against its pinned dependency versions installed in my scratchpad; first I checked that this setup does catch type errors.

(1) Booking past capacity. The admin "New reservation" dialog now handles 409 SLOT_FULL when an overbook is allowed. It shows the server's message and asks for a reason (3–300 characters), plus a manager PIN only when managerRequired is true. It then sends the same booking again with { overbook: true, overbookReason, managerOverridePin }, the field names the server uses. Afterwards it says which table the booking got, or that it was booked past capacity with no table yet. A wrong PIN, a PIN lockout or a missing PIN is shown in the same words as the petty-cash page. The logic lives in a React-free file, frontend/admin/src/app/reservations/overbook.ts, so it can be tested. The tablet host screen had no way to create a booking at all, so there was nothing to show the prompt on. I added a small "New booking" sheet to the existing screen: brand, name, phone, party size, time today or walk-in now, notes. It uses the same POST /reservations with the same overbook prompt and wording, and shows the assigned table.

(2) SMTP password at rest. PUT /auth/integrations/email now encrypts the password with lib/secretBox when SERVD_SECRET_KEY is set. An existing plain-text password is encrypted the first time it is read, using a conditional update like the WhatsApp key. Without the key, saving still works in plain text and is never blocked; the reply then includes passAtRest: 'plaintext' and a warning. An encrypted password the server cannot read is never sent as the password: sending falls back to the SMTP_PASS environment variable. GET returns passSet, passAtRest and passSource, never the password or any part of it. /health has a new smtpPassAtRest check with the same levels and wording as whatsappKeyAtRest: ok / warn / off. The save now writes all fields in one transaction. In auth/routes.ts and index.ts I loaded the new mailer functions with a dynamic import inside the handlers, so I didn't touch the import lines outside my areas.

(3) Fiscal screens (NEEDS 23). connectorsApi.ts now types heldNote and the reporting switch's reply (heldCount, heldNote). Error text now has plain words for REPORTING_OFF, NOT_LIVE, TOTALS_MISMATCH, FISCAL_IN_DOUBT and NOT_RETRYABLE. Status reasons have readable labels. New helpers spot documents held back because their totals don't match, including the case where an earlier send's result is unknown. heldNote is shown on the Status tab, Fiscal setup (switch card and the warning banner), the POS page banner and the overview card. The Held counter's small print changes while reporting is off. "Release all held" is greyed out with the reason while reporting is off. The switch shows what happened after saving. In Submissions, these documents get a red "Figures do not add up — not sent" mark with the steps to take, a banner when any are listed, and a box in the document drawer; the "result unknown" case says to press Retry first and not file by hand. docs/TAX_SETUP.md §2 has a new section on switching "Fiscal reporting required" off and back on (held sales, /health, release). I also added troubleshooting rows for REPORTING_OFF, NOT_LIVE and totals mismatch, and a note on SMTP encryption and rollback in §4 step 0.

built.prodNotes: Deploy order: there is no schema change or migration. The backend and admin can ship together; the admin tolerates an older API because heldNote is optional. Production has no SERVD_SECRET_KEY yet, so the SMTP password stays in plain text and email keeps working. /health will show a new smtpPassAtRest: 'warn' (HTTP 200, not an outage) until the key is set. Once SERVD_SECRET_KEY is set on the API container, the stored SMTP password is encrypted the first time it is read (sending, the email settings page, or /health). ROLLBACK CAVEAT: once that has happened, an API image older than this release reads the stored value as-is and sends the ciphertext as the SMTP password, so email (password-reset mails, backup codes) breaks. After such a rollback, re-enter the SMTP password in Configuration → Email straight away. This is the same as the existing WhatsApp-key caveat, and is now noted in TAX_SETUP.md §4 step 0 and in the mailer.ts header. Once the key is set, never change or lose it: an encrypted password then can't be read, sending falls back to the SMTP_PASS environment variable, and /health warns.

review.title: Tablet 'New booking' sheet: its default time is always refused (TOO_SOON), and it can only book later today
review.scenario: The sheet sends source 'staff' (anything except a walk-in) with startTime = today at nextQuarterPkt(), which is at most 15 minutes away. POST /reservations applies the company's reservation policy to every source except 'walkin' (reservations/routes.ts ~338-352). minAdvanceHours defaults to 2 (schema @default(2)). Reproduced on servd_test_r5_o_rv with the sheet's exact body: 400 TOO_SOON, 'Reservations must be made at least 2 hours in advance.' So a host who opens the sheet and presses Book with the default time is refused with no explanation, before the capacity check runs, which means the overbook prompt the sheet was added for never appears. The time field is also locked to today: phone bookings for tomorrow or later are impossible, and after about 22:00 PKT no scheduled booking can be made at all (nextQuarterPkt also caps at 23:45, which can be in the past). The feature only really works for walk-ins, or for times at least 2 hours later today. The builder's tests and report don't mention this.
review.fix: Either remove the sheet (the builder's own owner question), or make it usable: add a date field; default the time to now + the policy's minAdvanceHours, rounded up to the next quarter hour (or read GET /setup/reservation-policy); and show TOO_SOON / TOO_FAR / PARTY_TOO_LARGE / WALKINS_DISABLED in plain words, e.g. 'Bookings need at least N hours' notice — use Walk-in for a party seating now'. Add a test that builds the sheet's default body and expects a 201 or a SLOT_FULL prompt, never TOO_SOON.

review.title: Totals-mismatch advice in Submissions: the 'result unknown' case and refunds promise a Retry the server can't do, and a refund is then told to file by hand
review.scenario: The outbox only marks a mismatch 'in doubt' (lastError 'TOTALS_MISMATCH (an earlier submit's outcome is unknown)…') when the vendor may already hold the document and was not confirmed absent. Since a failed lookup returns earlier through applyFailure, in practice that means the driver has no lookup capability (outbox.ts ~646-690). mismatchAdvice() tells the operator 'Press Retry first — servd asks the fiscal POS before anything else. Do NOT file it on the authority portal until the fiscal POS confirms it never got it'. On Retry: (a) for a SALE, lookupBeforeRebuild returns 'unresolved: this fiscal POS cannot be asked about a document', so every Retry gives 409 FISCAL_IN_DOUBT and the advice leads to a dead end; (b) for a REFUND, retryMismatch never looks up (rebuild/lookup is sale-only, ~853-856) and re-checks the unchanged stored payload, so it always answers 409 TOTALS_MISMATCH. connectorErrorText('TOTALS_MISMATCH') then shows '…file it on the authority portal and use Record manual filing', the opposite of the in-doubt warning on the same row. That invites a duplicate credit note when the fiscal POS already filed it. Separately, the non-in-doubt advice says Retry 'rebuilds the sale from the order and checks again'. For a refund document, Retry re-checks the same frozen payload and can never pass, so 'fix the order, then Retry' cannot work for refunds.
review.fix: In FiscalSubmissions, when a Retry fails on a row where isMismatchInDoubt(row) is true, show the in-doubt text instead of connectorErrorText's 'file it by hand' line. Make mismatchAdvice depend on kind: for a refund, say Retry only re-checks the stored figures, so use Record manual filing (or, when in doubt, confirm with the fiscal POS vendor first). For in-doubt rows, say that this fiscal POS can't be asked automatically and the vendor must confirm outside servd before anyone files by hand. Add helper tests for a refund row and an in-doubt row.

fix.summary:
Both review findings were real. The code fixes were already in the working tree from an earlier pass, and I checked each against the server. O-RV-1 already had route tests; O-RV-2 had no tests for a refund row, an in-doubt row, or the text shown after a failed Retry, so I added them. I also updated one older assertion that still expected the wording from before O-RV-2.

O-RV-1 (tablet/app/(staff)/reservations.tsx, frontend/admin/src/app/reservations/overbook.ts + page.tsx): the New booking sheet now has a date field with Today and Tomorrow buttons. It reads GET /setup/reservation-policy for the active company, and its default slot is now + minAdvanceHours + 5 minutes, rounded up to the next quarter hour. Late at night it rolls to tomorrow instead of stopping at 23:45. TOO_SOON, TOO_FAR, PARTY_TOO_LARGE and WALKINS_DISABLED are shown in plain words that point to Walk-in. The admin dialog shows the same words. Its default stays the selected date at 19:00, which the reviewer did not flag.

O-RV-2 (frontend/admin/src/lib/connectorsApi.ts, components/connectors/FiscalSubmissions.tsx): the advice now depends on the kind of document and on whether it is in doubt.
- A sale that is not in doubt: Retry rebuilds it from the order; if it still fails, file it by hand.
- A refund: Retry only re-checks the stored figures, so file it by hand and use Record manual filing.
- An in-doubt row: servd cannot ask this fiscal POS, so the vendor must confirm outside servd before anyone files it by hand.
The new retryErrorText() replaces connectorErrorText for Retry failures in the Submissions list and the document drawer. On an in-doubt row it never says "file it on the authority portal", whether Retry answers FISCAL_IN_DOUBT (a sale) or TOTALS_MISMATCH (a refund). On a refund it says Retry cannot rebuild it.

Nothing was rejected.

items.note: Confirmed: the old default (the next quarter hour today) gets 400 TOO_SOON; the route test proves it. Fix (already in the tree): a date field, a default slot of now + the policy's notice + 5 minutes rounded up to the quarter hour that rolls to tomorrow at night, and plain words for TOO_SOON, TOO_FAR, PARTY_TOO_LARGE and WALKINS_DISABLED. Tests in backend/tests/opsRound5.test.ts take the tablet's helper block out of the .tsx and run it against the real POST /reservations. Two companies: A requires 5 hours' notice, B the default 2. The sheet's default slot gets 201 or the SLOT_FULL prompt, never TOO_SOON, including with the form left open 4 minutes. Tomorrow books. A slot that clears B's 2 hours is TOO_SOON for A's brand. Walk-ins skip the notice period, and A's walk-ins-off switch does not affect B. Party too large and too far ahead are refused in plain words.

Confirmed against outbox.ts retryMismatch: on a no-lookup fiscal POS an in-doubt sale always gets 409 FISCAL_IN_DOUBT, and a refund always gets 409 TOTALS_MISMATCH because a refund is never looked up or rebuilt. Fix (already in the tree): mismatchAdvice depends on the kind (refund: only re-checks, so file by hand) and on in-doubt (the vendor must confirm outside servd). retryErrorText(err, row) is used for Retry failures in FiscalSubmissions (list and drawer). NEW tests in opsRound5.test.ts: helper tests for sale, refund and in-doubt sale/refund rows under both error codes, plus the fallback. Real-route tests on POST /connectors/fiscal/documents/:id/retry, with the test driver's lookup switched off: a refund mismatch gets 409 TOTALS_MISMATCH and the screen says file it by hand, not fix the order. An in-doubt sale gets 409 FISCAL_IN_DOUBT, the screen says ask the vendor and never file first, and nothing is rebuilt. An in-doubt refund gets 409 TOTALS_MISMATCH and still shows the in-doubt words; the test also shows that connectorErrorText alone would have said file it by hand. Company B gets 404 on A's documents. Updated one older assertion that expected the wording from before O-RV-2.

built.summary:
Stream T is done. A manager can now refund the card payment on a cancelled or rejected ticket back to the card, on the card machine. The refund can't be more than the ticket still owes back by card, after taking off refunds already booked and card-machine refunds still in progress (including ones stuck waiting for a manager). It is booked once, as the cancelled-ticket hand-back entry in the order's own company, and no fiscal document is created.

Backend, pos/service.ts:
- assertRefundAllowed now accepts cancelled and rejected orders. For those it checks the amount against what the ticket still owes back, by the tender that took it, after card-machine refunds still in progress. Completed orders go through exactly the same checks as before.
- refundDueOnCancelledTicket now counts card-machine refunds still in progress, both before the order lock and again under it. So recording a card hand-back by hand can't give the same money back a second time.
- When it books a card-machine refund, it first looks for a refund row already booked for that card-machine refund. If it finds one it returns that row and posts nothing new, so a lapsed booking lease can't book it twice.
- The audit entry now names the card-machine refund.
- The NOTHING_TO_REFUND message now also covers money that is already on its way back to the card.

Backend, connectors/terminal/service.ts (startTerminalRefund):
- Completed, cancelled and rejected orders are accepted, both before and under the lock. Every other status still gets 409 NOT_REFUNDABLE.
- Under the lock it checks whether a refund with the same idempotency key was just created, and it catches the duplicate-key error. Two taps with the same key push one refund to the machine and both get the same answer (201 and 200).
- When the amount is too much for a cancelled ticket (REFUND_EXCEEDS_DUE or NOTHING_TO_REFUND), the answer is 409 AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_REFUNDABLE.
- Every existing guard is kept: the route is still managers-only, foreign rows still 404, only card-machine payments, per-payment cap, refund policy (reason, photo, caps) checked before the machine moves money, refunds are never reversed.

Admin:
- tillApi.ts has a new pure helper, cancelledCardRefundOffer. It decides whether "Refund to card" is offered and the most it can be. It uses the same rule as the server: refund due, card still owed, what's left on that card payment, and refunds in progress. fetchCancelledCardRefundOffer loads the order, its card-machine charges and whether a card machine is connected. ZReportExtras.cancelledPaid has an optional orderIds field.
- The shift page's Z-report "Refund due" box now lists each cancelled ticket that took card money. For managers, each row has a "Refund to card" button with amount and reason, using the existing refundOnCardMachine flow and its progress text.
- The per-ticket rows need the Z report to send orderIds. Until it does, the box shows a one-line hint, and non-managers are told to ask a manager.

review.title: Two card-machine refunds on one cancelled ticket, booked at the same time: the second is refused after the card was already refunded (needs_attention, money back but not booked)
review.scenario: Reproduced in 2 of 3 runs on servd_test_r5_t_rv. Setup: a cancelled ticket took 80,000 by card on the machine. A manager starts R1 for 40,000 and R2 for 40,000; both starts pass, since R2's start counts R1 as in flight. The machine approves both, and recordApprovedCharge(R1) and recordApprovedCharge(R2) run together (a webhook plus a staff poll or the reconciler retry). R1's booking transaction commits its refund Payment, but R1's TerminalCharge is only set to recorded / paymentId in a separate updateMany AFTER that commit (terminal/service.ts:535). R2 was waiting on the order lock and wakes up inside that gap. refundDueOnCancelledTicket then counts R1 twice: once as a booked refund in refundDueOf.alreadyRefunded, and again in inFlightTerminalRefundCents, because R1 is still 'approved' with paymentId null and only R2 itself is excluded. Due becomes 80,000 - 40,000 - 40,000 = 0, so R2 fails with NOTHING_TO_REFUND. R2 is marked needs_attention and an alert says 'Card refund given but not booked': the customer has the money back but the ledger does not show it, and someone has to fix it by hand. The same double count also makes a start, or a record-only cash hand-back, inside that gap refuse a legitimate amount for a moment. Repro test: start two 40k refunds, set both to approved, run Promise.all(ids.map(recordApprovedCharge)). Expected both 'recorded'; got ['recorded','needs_attention' / NOTHING_TO_REFUND]. The completed-sale refundOrder path has the same pattern from before, but this stream added it to the cancelled-ticket booking.
review.fix: In the in-flight count, leave out refund charges that already have a booked refund Payment. Either collect the gatewayMeta.terminalChargeId values of current.payments with status 'refunded' and pass them as excluded ids to inFlightTerminalRefundCents (in refundDueOnCancelledTicket under the lock, in its pre-check, and in assertRefundAllowed / startTerminalRefund), or stamp the charge's paymentId/status inside the booking transaction. Add a regression test with two concurrent recordApprovedCharge calls on one cancelled ticket, and ideally the same for the completed path.

review.title: 'Refund to card' UI (T-9) cannot be reached, and the shift-page hint sends managers to a button that does not exist
review.scenario: getZReport (pos/service.ts ~1392) still returns cancelledPaid without orderIds. So CancelledCardRefunds always takes the orderIds === null branch, and the per-ticket rows and button never render. The hint it shows says 'a manager opens the ticket and uses Refund to card'. But orders/[id]/page.tsx MoneyTakenModal has no card-machine option: it calls only refundThroughEngine, which is record-only, and refundOnCardMachine is not used there. That change is deferred to stream K. After this stream, no screen can start a card-machine refund on a cancelled ticket, yet T-9 is reported 'fixed'. The box also only appears in the Z report shown right after the drawer is closed. It keys on cancelledPaid.cardCents, which is the gross card taken, so the hint still shows when all the card money has already been handed back. The one-line backend change needed (orderIds: sales.cancelledPaid.orderIds) is in pos/service.ts, a file this stream already edits.

fix.summary:
Both review findings were real and both are fixed. Nothing was rejected.

T-RV-1 (two card-machine refunds booked at the same moment on one ticket): I fixed it in the one shared count, `inFlightTerminalRefundCents` in backend/src/modules/pos/service.ts. Before it adds up the refund charges that are still on their way back, it now reads the order's refund payments. Any charge named in a payment's `gatewayMeta.terminalChargeId` is already booked, so it is left out, along with `exceptChargeId`. A refund that is booked but whose charge has not been stamped yet (the gap after the booking commits and before `recordApprovedCharge` stamps the charge) is now counted once, not twice. Every caller picks this up: the booking under the lock and its pre-check in `refundDueOnCancelledTicket`, the start check in `startTerminalRefund` / `assertRefundAllowed`, the record-only hand-back, and the completed-sale `refundOrder` path, which had the same problem before this stream. I did not move the stamp inside the booking transaction, because the count fix covers every caller with one change.

T-RV-2 (the "Refund to card" rows could never appear): `getZReport` now returns `cancelledPaid.orderIds` and a new `cancelledPaid.cardOwedCents`. That figure is this drawer's card takings on the cancelled tickets, less every card refund on those tickets, floored at zero per ticket. Machine refunds that are not booked yet are not deducted; the per-row offer still checks them. The per-ticket rows and the "Refund to card" button on the shift Z report now render. The box shows only while card money is still owed back. It uses a new pure helper, `cancelledCardStillOwed()` in tillApi.ts, which falls back to gross card taken for an older API. The hint shown when there is no ticket list no longer points to a button on the ticket page. It now says: refund it on the card machine, then record it on the ticket as a card hand-back.

T-9 is still partial. The button exists only on the Z report shown right after the drawer is closed. The order page has no card-machine option until stream K ships it.

Files changed: backend/src/modules/pos/service.ts (`inFlightTerminalRefundCents` and the cancelled-ticket part of `getZReport`), frontend/admin/src/components/pos/tillApi.ts (the `ZReportExtras.cancelledPaid` type and the `cancelledCardStillOwed` helper), frontend/admin/src/app/pos/shift/page.tsx (the condition for showing the box and the hint text), and backend/tests/cancelledCardRefund.test.ts.

items.note: Real. inFlightTerminalRefundCents (pos/service.ts) now leaves out refund charges that already have a booked refund Payment (gatewayMeta.terminalChargeId), so a charge in the gap between the booking commit and its stamp is not counted twice. The fix sits in the one shared count, so it covers the cancelled-ticket booking and its pre-check, startTerminalRefund / assertRefundAllowed, the record-only hand-back, and the completed-sale refundOrder path. Tests: a deterministic gap test (R1 booked but its charge still approved; R2 recordApprovedCharge comes back 'recorded', not needs_attention); inside the gap, a legitimate record-only hand-back and a machine start are allowed while one paisa over is refused; 4 rounds of Promise.all on two approved 40k refunds; the same gap on a completed sale; and a two-company check that B's booked refunds never change A's count. With the fix switched off, 3 of the new tests fail.

Real. getZReport.cancelledPaid now returns orderIds and cardOwedCents. The shift page shows the box only while cancelledCardStillOwed() is true, using card still owed rather than gross card taken. The no-orderIds hint now says to refund on the card machine and record it on the ticket as a card hand-back. Test: the Z report lists both cancelled tickets; cardOwedCents goes 70,000 → 0 after a machine refund plus a record-only hand-back while gross cardCents stays 70,000; the helper switches to false; B's manager gets 404 on A's drawer; the older-API fallback is covered. T-9 should be reported as PARTIAL: the button exists only on the Z report shown right after close, and the order page has no card-machine option until stream K ships it.
